summary: EfficientNet-B5 paired-view Phase 3 v1 run using full images plus 456px crops, task_gated_residual fusion, crop_prior initialization, lr=5e-5, backbone_lr_scale=0.1, batch_size=2, grad_accum_steps=12, cosine scheduler, and unfrozen Phase 1/2 heads. The run warm-started from outputs/data2/b5_pair_v2/phase2/best_model_phase2.pth and activated all 16 tasks: the 7 existing Phase 1/2 tasks plus the 9 locked Phase 3 fields. Training requested 20 epochs but early-stopped after epoch 6 because validation loss only improved at epoch 1. Best overall accuracy was 58.21% at epoch 4; best validation loss was 1.1451 at epoch 1. Phase 3 visual fields learned meaningful signal, especially roof_materials, window, entrance, wall_features, landscape_features, and building_category. However, Phase 1/2 retention dropped materially versus the Phase 2 paired-v2 checkpoint, especially primary_cladding, stories, setting, and roof_type. Use this run as a successful Phase 3 integration proof and diagnostic baseline, not as the new production model over paired-v2 Phase 2.

checkpoint_selection.checkpoint_epoch5.pth: Periodic checkpoint at epoch 5. No epoch 6 checkpoint was written because periodic checkpointing is every 5 epochs.

results.trend: Training loss decreased every epoch from 0.4557 to 0.3659, showing the model continued fitting. Validation loss was best immediately after epoch 1 and then rose to 1.2603 by epoch 6, while overall accuracy peaked at epoch 4 and stayed essentially tied at epoch 6. Phase 3 visual tasks generally improved from epoch 1 through epoch 4-6, but old-task retention weakened enough that this run is not an automatic replacement for the Phase 2 checkpoint.

vs_b5_pair_v2_phase2_best_accuracy.overall: Not directly comparable as a single headline because Phase 3 overall averages 16 tasks while Phase 2 averaged 7 tasks. Phase 3 best overall was 58.21% across 16 tasks; Phase 2 best overall was 76.22% across 7 tasks.
vs_b5_pair_v2_phase2_best_accuracy.architectural_style: -2.21 percentage_points at best Phase 3 epoch (71.34% vs 73.55%). Moderate retention loss.
vs_b5_pair_v2_phase2_best_accuracy.stories: -10.88 percentage_points (62.74% vs 73.62%). Significant retention loss; stories remains the main crop-preservation risk.
vs_b5_pair_v2_phase2_best_accuracy.roof_type: -6.00 percentage_points (56.11% vs 62.10%). Crop-heavy defaults helped avoid total collapse but did not preserve the Phase 2 level.
vs_b5_pair_v2_phase2_best_accuracy.primary_cladding: -12.12 percentage_points (65.58% vs 77.70%). This is the largest old-task regression and likely reflects Phase 3 multitask pressure plus cladding's known sensitivity to scale/context.
vs_b5_pair_v2_phase2_best_accuracy.setting_exact: -8.99 percentage_points (65.79% vs 74.78%). Full-heavy routing did not preserve setting enough in this 16-task run.
vs_b5_pair_v2_phase2_best_accuracy.chimney_present: -5.66 percentage_points (88.68% vs 94.34%). Still high accuracy, but imbalance makes accuracy easier than macro F1.

phase3_task_signal.strongest_visual_fields: roof_materials reached 90.76% Jaccard at epoch 4 and 89.00% at epoch 6, but macro F1 stayed around 34%, so dominant labels are likely doing much of the work. Window reached 41.58% Jaccard and 47.82% macro F1 by epoch 6. Entrance reached 40.15% Jaccard and 40.75% macro F1 by epoch 6. Wall and landscape features reached roughly 34-40% Jaccard with 40% and 37% macro F1 respectively.
phase3_task_signal.context_fields: building_category is learnable at 94.88-95.13% accuracy with 63-65% macro F1. Associated_buildings is partial: exact match around 29-33%, Jaccard 28-32%, macro F1 around 19-22%.
phase3_task_signal.weak_use_fields: current_use and original_use are weak but not hopeless. At best accuracy, current_use was 32.06% accuracy / 25.55% macro F1 and original_use was 39.74% accuracy / 35.62% macro F1. Original_use improved to 41.82% / 35.99% by epoch 6, while current_use remained near 31% / 26%.

comparison.vs_step5_capped_200: The capped 200-batch trial was directionally optimistic but overestimated retention and some Phase 3 metrics. Full validation shows lower old-task retention and lower use-field performance, while confirming that the direct visual Phase 3 fields are learnable.

learnings: Phase 3 wiring is validated end-to-end: all 16 heads train, validate, log metrics, and save checkpoints correctly from the paired-v2 Phase 2 warm start.
The nine new heads add real learnable signal, especially for direct visual multi-label fields: wall_features, landscape_features, window, entrance, roof_materials, and building_category.

The current Phase 3 multitask weighting is still too disruptive for Phase 1/2 retention. Even with conservative new-task weights and backbone_lr_scale=0.1, stories, primary_cladding, roof_type, and setting regress materially versus the Phase 2 checkpoint.

Best loss and best accuracy diverged again. Best loss was epoch 1, while best overall accuracy was epoch 4. After epoch 1, validation loss rose despite some task metrics improving, so checkpoint choice should remain metric-aware rather than loss-only.
current_use and original_use are image-weak targets. They produce some signal, especially original_use macro F1 around 35-36%, but they are not ready to drive model selection or high-weight training.
roof_materials looks deceptively strong by exact/Jaccard because the dominant labels are easy. Macro F1 around 34% means per-label analysis is required before treating this as solved.

Phase 3 should likely be trained with stronger protection for old heads or a staged strategy: first learn Phase 3 heads with the backbone mostly frozen or very slow, then unfreeze carefully. Full freezing failed in earlier Phase 2 work, but this run shows the opposite extreme still allows too much old-task drift.
next_steps: Keep outputs/data2/b5_pair_v2/phase2/best_model_phase2.pth as the production/comparison checkpoint for Phase 1/2 until a Phase 3 run matches retention requirements.
Use outputs/data2/phase3_full_v1/phase3/best_model_phase3.pth as the diagnostic Phase 3 v1 checkpoint for field-level evaluation, not as the replacement production model.

Run a Phase 3 v2 retention experiment with stronger old-task protection: reduce Phase 3 loss weights further or temporarily train only the nine Phase 3 heads while freezing old heads and using a very low backbone LR, then unfreeze with differential LR.

Consider splitting Phase 3 into visual-direct and context/use stages. Train direct visual fields first (wall_features, landscape_features, window, entrance, associated_buildings, building_category, roof_materials), then evaluate current_use and original_use separately.

Run per-label reports for multi-label Phase 3 tasks, especially roof_materials, window, entrance, wall_features, and associated_buildings. Jaccard alone hides which labels are learned versus dominated by common labels.
Before another full run, decide whether current_use and original_use should stay in the shared run at very low weights, move to a separate experiment, or wait for the 70k-building data drop.

If preserving stories and primary_cladding is mandatory, test stronger crop bypass/preservation for stories plus lower full-residual influence on primary_cladding, or reduce backbone updates further below backbone_lr_scale=0.1.
operational_notes: The run completed with exit code 0 and early-stopped after epoch 6 under early_stopping_patience=5.
The output directory contains best_model_phase3.pth, best_model_by_loss_phase3.pth, checkpoint_epoch5.pth, run_config.json, training_history.json, and this run_notes.json.

The saved run_config.json records git_commit 632eabd, which predates some uncommitted Phase 3 implementation changes in the working tree. Interpret this commit field as the repository HEAD at run start, not a fully clean committed provenance marker.
Large .pth files remain ignored by git. Only run_config.json, training_history.json, and run_notes.json should be considered for lightweight run documentation if committing outputs.
